app/src/api.ts:3-5 — API_BASE_URL normalization and cache policy centralized in one module; app/src/views/home.tsx:13 PAGE_SIZE single constant
app/src/views/home.tsx:22-29 — homeUrl() single canonical URL builder shared by full and partial responses, so filter state cannot drift between them

churn_resistance.rationale: Structure is upgrade-friendly (centralized config, canonical URL builder, standard Hono APIs, view-model types like Card/MoveRow), but the biggest boundary — the PokeAPI response shapes — is entirely 'any', so upstream or spec drift surfaces as runtime breakage rather than type errors, and data access is split between data.ts and view-local loaders.

findings.issue: API responses cross the type boundary as 'any' (api<T = any>, apiUrl<T = any>), with 16 downstream 'any' casts in data.ts and views; upstream shape changes break at runtime, not compile time.
findings.suggestion: Define response interfaces (Species, Pokemon, Move, Type…) in api.ts/data.ts and type the loaders' returns; tsc --noEmit already exists as a script.

findings.issue: Upstream fetch has no timeout or abort: a hung PokeAPI request holds the page render indefinitely with no recovery.
findings.suggestion: Use fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) }) and map aborts to a 502/500 page so users aren't left waiting.

findings.issue: View modules import api/apiUrl directly (also views/pokemon.tsx:1), so API path strings are spread across api.ts, data.ts and view loaders instead of one data-access layer.
findings.suggestion: Move loadMove/loadAbility/loadType/loadPokemon/loadMoves behind data.ts (or a dedicated loaders module) so views consume typed view models only.

findings.issue: In-memory cache is an unbounded Map with no eviction; only the fixed 30s freshness policy (FRESH_MS) limits work, not memory.
findings.suggestion: Cap entries with a simple LRU or periodic sweep; fine for the current snapshot but a leak against a live API with 100k+ move/species URLs.

findings.issue: serveStatic({ root: './dist' }) is resolved against process.cwd(); running the built server from any other directory silently breaks /static/*.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the static root relative to the built file (e.g. new URL('../static', import.meta.url)) or a documented absolute path.

findings.issue: hx-sync="this:replace" on the form is redundant with hx-sync="closest form:replace" on the inputs; harmless but duplicated configuration.
findings.suggestion: Keep the form-level hx-sync only (inputs already inherit the nearest sync strategy) to avoid two places to update when the strategy changes.

findings.issue: Exact version pins (no ^ ranges) for all deps; deliberate upgrades are required for every patch, including security fixes (the Sept 2026 serve-static fixes arrived in 2.1.3).
findings.suggestion: Use caret ranges with the lockfile (package-lock.json already pins exactly) or add a Dependabot/Renovate config so security patches aren't a manual edit.

summary: A deliberately modern, lean server-rendered app: every dependency is at the exact latest npm stable (Hono 4.13.14, node-server 2.1.5, htmx 2.0.11, TypeScript 7 native), and it uses the current documented Hono and htmx idioms — jsxRenderer, HX-Push-Url, hx-sync — with zero hand-rolled client JS. The main thing that will age badly is the fully untyped PokeAPI boundary ('any' throughout) and missing upstream fetch timeouts. Everything else — centralized config, canonical URL builders, single cache module — is set up to absorb framework upgrades with minimal churn.
